page: Microsoft Azure FX48-24mds_v2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the FXmdsv2 server family. Powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor with 12 physical cores and 24 vCPUs running at a high base clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The CPU architecture is x86_64, supported by a 260 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 1008.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 42.0 GB per physical core. Additionally, the server includes 2835 GB of local storage and is premium storage capable, though it does not feature any GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data highlights strong single-core and text processing capabilities. The server achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 2339.0 and a text processing score of 2938.0, both placing in the top tier (top 10%). Single-threaded gzip compression at 34.71 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.24 GB/sec rank in the top 25%. Multi-core performance is also robust, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 16414.0 (top 25%) and a stress-ng multi-core CPU performance of 26642.26 (middle 50%). Memory bandwidth is measured at 2070.85 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 186.82 GB/sec for large-block reads.

Given the high memory density of over 1 TB RAM alongside a high-frequency 4.2 GHz CPU, this server offers a specialized hardware profile. The combination of massive memory capacity and fast single-core execution makes it highly efficient for memory-intensive workloads that also require rapid sequential processing. Tradeoffs include the lack of GPU acceleration, which limits its utility for deep learning workloads. The server is designed for large-scale databases, in-memory analytics, heavy text processing, and memory-intensive enterprise applications.
